words.gloss: of mustard (sārṣapa; mustard, Brassica species; probable), qualifying the preceding taila

hindi: शहद का, तैल का, फलाह्वय का, क्षार का और सार्षप यानी सरसों के तैल का।
english: Of honey, of oil (taila), of phalāhvaya, of kṣāra, and of mustard (sārṣapa) oil.
notes: GROUPING: continues unit 36 (previous chunk: the preparation 'mixed with mustard oil, madana, kuṣṭha, akṣa-measures and prasṛtas'); 37 is a list of genitives with no governing word of its own, and 38 then names the people for whom the nirūha is given; how 37 relates to 38 is not stated, so no verb or measure word is supplied. 'phalāhvaya' is literally 'fruit-named' (a name derived from 'fruit'); no identification is made. 'tailasya sārṣapasya' is read as 'of mustard oil'; the first tailasya is a plain 'oil'. Mustard: Brassica species (probable). kṣāra is kept as the Sanskrit term.

words.gloss: for one afflicted with Kapha disease (kapharogin); the printed form is irregular
slow; fire (agni); for one with slow digestive fire (mandāgni; weak digestion, standard)
food; hater; for one who has aversion to food

hindi: कफ के रोग से पीड़ित को, मन्द अग्नि वाले को और भोजन से द्वेष रखने वाले को निरूह यानी काढ़े की बस्ति देनी चाहिए।
english: One should give the nirūha (decoction enema) to one afflicted with Kapha disease, to one with slow digestive fire (mandāgni), and to one with aversion to food.
notes: GROUPING: 37 and 38 continue the sentence of 36; 38 completes a first group of indications. 'kapharogitāya' is as printed and fits the metre (a dative of kapharogin would be 'kapharogiṇe'); the printed form looks like a metrical stretch and is read as 'for one afflicted with Kapha disease' without a flag. 'aśanavidviṣe' is the dative of a noun vidviṣ 'hater', hence 'aversion to food' (literally 'one who hates food'). Modern equivalents: nirūha = decoction enema (standard); mandāgni = weak digestion (standard).

words.gloss: punarnavā (spreading hogweed, Boerhavia diffusa; standard); eraṇḍa (castor, Ricinus communis; standard); bṛhatī (probably Indian nightshade, Solanum indicum; probable); aśmabheda (probably Bergenia ligulata, rock-foil; disputed); vṛścīva (identity disputed); bhūtīka (identity disputed); balā (country mallow, Sida cordifolia; standard); palāśa (flame-of-the-forest, Butea monosperma; standard)

hindi: पुनर्नवा यानी साठी, एरण्ड यानी अरण्डी, बृहती यानी प्रायः बड़ी कटेरी, अश्मभेद यानी सम्भवतः पाषाणभेद, वृश्चीव, भूतीक, बला यानी बरियार और पलाश यानी ढाक को।
english: Punarnavā (spreading hogweed), eraṇḍa (castor), bṛhatī (probably Indian nightshade), aśmabheda (probably Bergenia), vṛścīva, bhūtīka, balā (country mallow) and palāśa (flame-of-the-forest).

text_flags.why: possible: punarnavā + eraṇḍa gives 'punarnavairaṇḍa'; the printed anusvāra after 'ai' looks stray; the doubled 't' in 'bṛhatty-' is only orthographic

notes: GROUPING: units 39 to 46 read as one sentence: 39 and 40 list ingredients, 41 adds more and the measure of the fruits, 42 the milk preparation, 43 to 45 the pastes and additions, and 46 gives the verb 'dadyāt nirūham'. 39 is an accusative list with no verb in the unit (the verb comes in 46). Orthography: 'punarnavaiṃraṃḍa' has a stray anusvāra after 'ai' (flagged); the doubled t in 'bṛhattyaśma' is an orthographic doubling (bṛhatī + aśmabheda). Identifications are written once here: punarnavā, eraṇḍa, balā and palāśa standard; bṛhatī probable (Solanum indicum; other Solanum species are also used); aśmabheda disputed (Bergenia ligulata is the usual choice, but other plants are also called aśmabheda); vṛścīva and bhūtīka disputed and not identified here.

words.gloss: dvipañcamūla (lit. two-fives roots: the ten roots, daśamūla; standard group)
pala (a unit of weight); share; (ones) with a pala as the share

hindi: और द्विपञ्चमूल यानी दशमूल, एक पल के भाग वाले, कुचले हुए, धोए हुए, और आठ फल।
english: And the dvipañcamūla (the ten roots), (ones) with a pala as the share, crushed (ones), washed (ones), and eight fruits.
notes: GROUPING: continues 39 (same sentence, verb in 46). The adjectives palāṃśakāni, kṣuṇṇāni, dhautāni are neuter plural, while dvipañcamūla is singular, so they may refer to the roots as plural items or to the whole list of 39 and 40; the Sanskrit does not settle this and the translation keeps the adjectives bare. The fruits are not named (no plant is supplied). Dvipañcamūla = daśamūla, the standard group of ten roots (standard); its members are not listed in the text.

words.gloss: yava (barley, Hordeum vulgare; standard); aṅkola (probably Alangium salvifolium; probable); kulattha (horse gram, Macrotyloma uniflorum; standard); dhānya (grain; coriander is a possible alternative, disputed)

hindi: बिल्व यानी बेल, यव, अङ्कोल यानी प्रायः ढेरा, कुलत्थ यानी कुल्थी और धान्य, और फल प्रसृत के माप के होने चाहिए।
english: Bilva (bael), yava (barley), aṅkola (probably Alangium), kulattha (horse gram) and dhānya (grain); and the fruits should be measured by prasṛtas (handful-measures).
notes: GROUPING: continues 40 (same sentence, verb in 46). It is not stated whether the bilva to dhānya group is also measured by a prasṛta, or whether 'phalāni' means the fruits of those plants; the translation follows the words only. 'dhānya' is read as 'grain' (the compound with yava and kulattha); 'coriander' (dhānyaka) would be a different reading and is not adopted. prasṛta is a measure of quantity (a handful); no weight is stated.

words.gloss: water; two; āḍhaka (a measure); prepared with
words.gram: tat-puruṣa, n. nom. sg., ppp. caus. √sidh

hindi: दूध, जो दो आढक जल के साथ तैयार किया गया है, उस दूध के शेष रहने वाला, स्वच्छ वस्त्र से छाना हुआ।
english: Milk prepared with two āḍhakas of water, that (preparation) with the milk remaining, strained through a clean cloth.
notes: GROUPING: continues 41 (same sentence, verb in 46). 'payas' can mean milk or water; here it is read as milk because jala 'water' is named separately and the compound 'tatkṣīrāvaśiṣṭa' speaks of that milk remaining. The Sanskrit says only 'prepared with two āḍhakas of water, the milk remaining'; it is not spelled out that the water is boiled away. āḍhaka is a unit of measure (large); no equivalent is given.

words.gloss: vacā (sweet flag, Acorus calamus; standard); śatāhvā (probably dill, Anethum sowa; probable); amaradāru (deodar cedar, Cedrus deodara; standard, = devadāru); kuṣṭha (costus root, Saussurea costus; standard); yaṣṭyāhva (liquorice, Glycyrrhiza glabra; standard); siddhārtha (white mustard, completed as siddhārthaka by the next token; probable)
-ka (completes the preceding siddhārtha as siddhārthaka; the printed word-division is probably wrong)

hindi: वचा यानी बच, शताह्वा यानी प्रायः सोया, अमरदारु यानी देवदारु, कुष्ठ यानी कूट, यष्ट्याह्व यानी मुलेठी, सिद्धार्थक यानी प्रायः सफेद सरसों और पिप्पली यानी पीपर के।
english: Of vacā (sweet flag), śatāhvā (probably dill), amaradāru (deodar cedar), kuṣṭha (costus), yaṣṭyāhva (liquorice), siddhārthaka (probably white mustard) and pippalī (long pepper).

text_flags.suggest: -ka pippalīnāṃ (ka joined to the preceding siddhārtha)
text_flags.why: possible: the metre (22 syllables) and the sense fit 'siddhārthaka' + 'pippalīnām'; 'kapippalī' is not a word (kapi-pippalī would need a long 'pip')

notes: GROUPING: continues 42 (same sentence); these genitives are the drugs of the pastes (kalkaiḥ) named in 44. Orthography: the edition writes 'śatāvhā' for śatāhvā (letters transposed); read as śatāhvā throughout, recorded here once and not flagged again. The printed space in 'siddhārtha kapippalīnāṃ' is read as a mis-division: siddhārthaka (white mustard) + pippalīnām; this fits the 22-syllable metre exactly (flagged as possible). Identifications written once here: vacā, amaradāru, kuṣṭha, yaṣṭyāhva, pippalī standard; śatāhvā and siddhārthaka probable (śatāhvā is dill, though fennel is sometimes meant).

words.gloss: madana fruits (emetic nut, Randia dumetorum; standard)
not; too; hot; cold: neither too hot nor too cold

hindi: कल्कों से, यवानी यानी अजवायन से और मदन यानी मैनफल से युक्त; न अधिक गरम न अधिक ठण्डा; गुड़ और सैन्धव यानी सेंधा नमक से लिप्त।
english: Joined with pastes (kalka), with yavānī (ajwain) and with madana (emetic nut) fruits; neither too hot nor too cold; smeared with jaggery (guḍa) and rock salt (saindhava).
notes: GROUPING: continues 43 (same sentence). The neuter nominatives (yuktam, āktam) agree with payaḥ of 42, the preparation to which the pastes of 43 and the additions of 44 and 45 are applied. 'āktam' is literally 'smeared, anointed'. Identifications: yavānī and madana standard; ajwain is the usual yavānī (the name is sometimes also applied to related seeds).

hindi: शहद के, तैल के और नए घी के तीन प्रसृतों के समूह से युक्त।
english: Joined with a set of three prasṛtis (handful-measures) of honey, of oil and of fresh ghee.
notes: GROUPING: continues 44 (same sentence, verb in 46). The three substances are in the genitive and 'prasṛtitraya' is an instrumental, so the literal sense is 'joined by a triad of prasṛtis, of honey, of oil and of fresh ghee'. Whether three prasṛtis are meant for each substance or three in all is not stated; the translation leaves it open. 'prasṛti' and 'prasṛta' are the same measure.

words.gloss: rule; knower: one who knows the rule

hindi: विधि को जानने वाला विधि से उस निरूह को दे, जो सबके संसर्ग से उत्पन्न आमयों का नाश करने वाला है।
english: One who knows the rule should give that nirūha (decoction enema) by the rule, the destroyer of ailments produced by the combination of all.
notes: GROUPING: ends the sentence that runs through 39 to 45 (the verb 'dadyāt' governs the nirūha prepared in those units). 'sarvasaṃsarga' is literally 'combination of all'; the text does not say of what, so nothing is added (it may refer to a combination of all the doṣas). 'āmaya' = ailment. 'tam' is the nirūha just described.

words.gram: tat-puruṣa, m. acc. pl., ppp. vi-√dhā

hindi: इसलिए आधे-आधे विधान किए गए बस्तियों को चित्र यानी विविध कहा जाता है।
english: Therefore they declare the bastis arranged half and half to be varied (citra).

text_flags.why: possible: 'drdha' looks like a transposition of 'rddha' (arddha-arddha); the compound 'half-half arranged' needs the second member arddha

notes: Reading: 'ardhārdhavihita' is taken as 'arranged by halves and halves'; what is halved is not stated (the following units give lists of drug groups), so the sense is left as the words say. 'ataḥ' can mean 'hence' or 'from here on'. A new topic begins here: units 48 onwards give lists of drugs; it is not stated which list belongs to which basti.

words.gloss: kośātakī (probably ridged gourd, Luffa acutangula; probable); dvyeśvāku (unclear in the print; unsplit); phala (fruit); jīmūta (probably jīmūtaka, bristly luffa, Luffa echinata; probable); vatsaka (kuṭaja, Holarrhena pubescens; standard; lit. 'calf')

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार: कोशातकी यानी प्रायः तोरई, द्व्येश्वाकु जो छपाई में अस्पष्ट है, फल, जीमूत यानी प्रायः देवदाली और वत्सक यानी कुटज।
english: On a conjectural reading: kośātakī (probably ridged gourd), dvyeśvāku (unclear in the print), fruit (phala), jīmūta (probably bristly luffa) and vatsaka (kuṭaja).

text_flags.why: possible: 'dvyeśvāku' is not a known word; 'dvyaikṣvāku' (two ikṣvākus) is conceivable but not certain

notes: GROUPING: 48 to 52 form one sentence (a list of drugs in 48 to 51, 'joined with paste and rock salt, cleansers of the pakvāśaya' in 52). 'dvyeśvāku' is not a clear word as printed: it may be a damaged form of 'dvyaikṣvāku' (two ikṣvākus, bitter gourds), but this is not sure, so it is left unsplit and unidentified. Whether 'phala' is the fruit of that plant or a separate item is not clear. kośātakī: Luffa acutangula is probable (the name is also applied to other Luffa species); jīmūta probably = jīmūtaka (Luffa echinata); vatsaka = kuṭaja (standard).

words.gloss: śyāmā (in the tradition the black kind of trivṛt; disputed, lit. 'dark'); trivṛt (turpeth, Operculina turpethum; standard)
dantī (probably Baliospermum montanum, wild croton; probable); dravantī (identity disputed); born of

hindi: श्यामा और त्रिवृत् यानी निशोथ का मूल, वैसे ही दन्ती यानी प्रायः जंगली जमालगोटा और द्रवन्ती से उत्पन्न।
english: The root of śyāmā and trivṛt (turpeth), and likewise (that) born of dantī (probably wild croton) and dravantī.
notes: GROUPING: continues 48 (same sentence, verb-less list). 'dantīdravantija' is 'born of dantī and dravantī'; the text does not say what is meant (it may be the root, as in the first half), so nothing is added. Identifications: trivṛt standard; śyāmā disputed (the black variety of trivṛt in the tradition, but it is listed beside trivṛt here); dantī probable (Baliospermum montanum); dravantī disputed.

words.gloss: kṣīriṇī (lit. 'milky'; identity disputed, several plants bear the name)

hindi: प्रकीर्या और उदकीर्या, क्षीरिणी, नीलिनी यानी प्रायः नील, फल।
english: Prakīryā and udakīryā, kṣīriṇī, nīlinī (probably indigo), fruit.
notes: GROUPING: continues 48 and 49 (same list). 'phalam' stands alone; it is probably the fruit of the preceding plant (nīlinī) or of the group, but the text does not say, so none is supplied. The tradition takes prakīryā and udakīryā as two different plants but their identity is disputed here; kṣīriṇī is disputed; nīlinī probable.

words.gloss: of kampillaka (kamala tree, Mallotus philippensis; standard)

hindi: समला, शङ्खिनी, रोध्र यानी लोध और कम्पिल्लक यानी कमीला का फल।
english: Samalā, śaṅkhinī, rodhra (lodhra), and the fruit of kampillaka (kamala tree).

text_flags.why: possible: the conjunct 'dhr' seems to have lost its 'r' (rodhra, lodhra); the same form recurs in unit 56

notes: GROUPING: continues 50, the list ends with 52. 'rodhaṃ' is printed with the r of the conjunct dropped (also in 56); it is read as rodhra (lodhra) and flagged as possible. Identifications: kampillaka and rodhra standard; samalā unidentified; śaṅkhinī disputed.

words.gloss: pakvāśaya (the seat of digested matter, the colon; standard); cleansers

hindi: कल्क और सैन्धव यानी सेंधा नमक से युक्त, पक्वाशय यानी बड़ी आँत को शुद्ध करने वाले।
english: (Ones) joined with paste (kalka) and rock salt (saindhava), cleansers of the pakvāśaya (the seat of digested matter, the colon).
notes: GROUPING: closes the sentence of 48 to 51; the verb 'are' is not in the Sanskrit and is not supplied. The masculine plural nominatives refer to the drugs listed in 48 to 51. pakvāśaya = the seat of digested (cooked) matter, i.e. the colon (standard).

words.gloss: dhātakī (woodfordia, Woodfordia fruticosa; standard); puṣpa (flower); takrīṃr (unclear in the print; unsplit); jīvantī (Leptadenia reticulata; probable); mūla (root); vatsaka (kuṭaja; see unit 48)

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार: धातकी के फूल, तक्रींर् जो छपाई में अस्पष्ट है, जीवन्ती की जड़ और वत्सक।
english: On a conjectural reading: dhātakī flowers, takrīṃr (unclear in the print), the root of jīvantī, and vatsaka.

text_flags.why: possible: 'dhātukī' for dhātakī (woodfordia flowers); u/a confusion
possible: 'takrīṃr' is not a word; the half-line is one syllable short and 'takrāmra' would fit the metre, but this is only a guess

notes: GROUPING: starts a new list (53 to 56) of drugs called 'saṃgrāhika' (binding) in 56. Two doubtful spots: the printed 'dhātukī' is read as dhātakī (the woodfordia, whose flowers are the usual drug; flagged), and 'takrīṃr' is not a word as printed. With a restored 'takrāmra' the half-line would have 16 syllables (the printed one has 15), but that reading is not sure, so the word is left unsplit and untranslated. Whether 'mūla' belongs to jīvantī only or to more items is not settled.

words.gloss: khadirī (probably an acacia of the khadira kind, Senegalia catechu; disputed)
śamī (Prosopis cineraria; probable); piṇḍītakā (identity disputed; piṇḍītaka is also a name of madana); yava (barley; see unit 41)

hindi: प्रग्रह, खदिरी, कुष्ठ यानी कूट, तथा शमी यानी प्रायः खेजड़ी, पिण्डीतका और यव।
english: Pragraha, khadirī, kuṣṭha (costus), and śamī (probably the khejri tree), piṇḍītakā, and yava (barley).
notes: GROUPING: continues 53 (list). 'pragraha' is taken as a drug name but may not be one (it can also mean 'restraint'); it is left unidentified. khadirī is disputed (probably a form of khadira, Senegalia catechu); śamī probable; piṇḍītakā disputed. 'yavāḥ' is a plural, so barley grains.

words.gloss: priyaṅgu (usually Callicarpa macrophylla; disputed); rakta (red); mūla (root); the case and number of 'mūle' (dual or locative) are uncertain
words.gram: n. nom. du. or loc. sg., reading uncertain

words.gloss: bhairaṇī (unidentified); jāti (jasmine, Jasminum grandiflorum; probable); yūthikā (Jasminum auriculatum; probable)

hindi: प्रियङ्गु और लाल जड़, तथा भैरणी, जाति यानी प्रायः चमेली और यूथिका यानी प्रायः जूही।
english: Priyaṅgu (disputed) and red root(s) (raktamūla; reading uncertain), and bhairaṇī, jāti (probably jasmine) and yūthikā (probably the yellow jasmine).
notes: GROUPING: continues 54 (list). 'priyaṅgurakta-mūle' is uncertain: it may name priyaṅgu and red roots (rakta-mūla, number unclear), but the grammar could also fit a different division; it is not identified. 'bhairaṇī' is not known (unidentified). The half-lines have 8 syllables each, so the text is metrically sound.

words.gloss: vaṭa (banyan, Ficus benghalensis; standard); beginning with
kiṃśuka (flame-of-the-forest, Butea monosperma, the palāśa of unit 39; standard)

hindi: वट आदि, किंशुक, रोध्र यानी लोध, इस प्रकार संग्राहिक यानी बाँधने वाले माने गए हैं।
english: Vaṭa and the rest, kiṃśuka, rodhra (lodhra): thus they are considered saṃgrāhika (binding).

text_flags.why: possible: 'rodha' for rodhra, as in unit 51

notes: GROUPING: closes the list of 53 to 56. The members of the vaṭa group are not given in the text. 'saṃgrāhikā matāḥ' is correct sandhi (āḥ before a voiced consonant). 'rodham' is printed without the r, as in 51 (flagged). 'iti' closes the list.

words.gloss: binding (grāhi); priyaṅgu (see unit 55); ambaṣṭhā (identity disputed, often equated with pāṭhā, Cissampelos pareira); and the rest; decoction (kvātha); pastes (kalka)
words.gram: dvandva and tat-puruṣa, m. inst. pl.

hindi: और क्रम से, ग्राही यानी बाँधने वाले प्रियङ्गु, अम्बष्ठा आदि के क्वाथों और कल्कों से।
english: And in sequence, with decoctions and pastes of the binding (grāhi) priyaṅgu, ambaṣṭhā and the rest.
notes: 'kātha' is a spelling of kvātha 'decoction' (the same count of syllables); the correction is flagged as possible. Whether 'grāhi' is an adjective ('binding priyaṅgu, ambaṣṭhā...') or names a group is not settled. The unit has no verb or noun for what is prepared; a continuation of the list of kinds begun at 47 is likely but not stated. ambaṣṭhā: disputed (the name is applied to several plants; often pāṭhā).

words.gloss: uṣaka (a saline earth; probable); and the rest; additive (pratīvāpa)
triphalā (the three myrobalans: harītakī, Terminalia chebula; bibhītaka, Terminalia bellirica; āmalaka, Phyllanthus emblica; standard); juice (rasa)

hindi: उषक आदि का प्रतीवाप, लेखन यानी खुरचने वाला त्रिफला यानी हरड़, बहेड़ा और आँवला का रस।
english: The additive (pratīvāpa) of uṣaka and the rest; the scraping (lekhana) triphalā juice.
notes: GROUPING: continues 57 (list of kinds). No noun such as basti is in the unit, so none is supplied; the unit reads as the description of a 'scraping' kind: its additive uṣaka and the rest, and the triphalā juice. uṣaka is taken as a saline earth (probable). triphalā = the three myrobalans (standard).

words.gloss: madhuka (probably liquorice, as yaṣṭyāhva in unit 43; the same name can mean mahua; probable)

hindi: मधुक यानी प्रायः मुलेठी के कल्क से और रस सहित घी से बृंहण यानी पुष्ट करने वाला।
english: Nourishing (bṛṃhaṇa), with a paste of madhuka (probably liquorice) and with ghee together with rasa.

text_flags.why: possible: 'kalkaina' is not a valid form; 'madhuka kalkena' (paste of madhuka) fits the sense and the metre

notes: GROUPING: continues 58 (list of kinds). 'madhuka kalkaina' is read as 'madhukakalkena' (a compound with a mis-division and a spurious 'ai'); flagged as possible. 'rasa' is kept as 'juice' (broth or juice; not specified). The unit has no noun for what is nourishing; none is supplied. madhuka: probable liquorice.

words.gloss: badarī (jujube, Ziziphus mauritiana; standard); airāvaṇī (unidentified); śailū (probably the Indian cherry, Cordia dichotoma; probable); śālmalī (silk-cotton tree, Bombax ceiba; standard); dhanvana (probably Grewia tiliifolia; probable); aṅkura (sprout, shoot)

hindi: बदरी यानी बेर, ऐरावणी, शैलू यानी प्रायः लसोड़ा, शाल्मली यानी सेमल और धन्वन यानी प्रायः धामिन के अंकुर।
english: The sprouts of badarī (jujube), airāvaṇī, śailū (probably the Indian cherry), śālmalī (silk-cotton tree) and dhanvana (probably Grewia).
notes: GROUPING: continues 59 (list of kinds); 60 and 61 form one statement ('aṅkurāḥ ... picchilāḥ smṛtāḥ'). 'aṅkurāḥ' is taken to govern all the names. airāvaṇī is unidentified.

hindi: शहद सहित, दूध से युक्त और रक्त सहित, पिच्छिल यानी चिपचिपे माने गए हैं।
english: (Ones) with honey, joined with milk and with blood are held to be slimy (picchila).
notes: GROUPING: continues 60 (same statement). The subject is the sprouts of 60. 'mākṣika' is taken as honey (it can also name a mineral). Whether 'picchila' here is a name for a kind is not stated; the words alone are given.

words.gloss: kola (jujube; probable; kola can also be a measure)

kataka (clearing nut, Strychnos potatorum; probable); kāṇḍekṣu (lit. 'stalk-cane'; identity disputed); darbha (kusha grass, Desmostachya bipinnata; standard); pāṭhā (velvet-leaf, Cissampelos pareira; probable); elavālu (conjectural correction of the printed 'eśuvālu'; identity unidentified)

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार: कोल यानी बेर, कतक यानी निर्मली, काण्डेक्षु, दर्भ यानी कुश, पाठा और एलवालु के साथ।
english: On a conjectural reading: jujube (kola) with kataka (clearing nut), kāṇḍekṣu, darbha (kusha grass), pāṭhā and elavālu.

text_flags.why: possible: 'pāṭheśuvālu' does not parse; 'pāṭhā' + 'elavālu' (ela/eśu look alike in the print) gives a plausible name and the right metre

notes: GROUPING: 62 and 63 go together ('dāhaghna' in 63; the first kind in 62 and the second with utpala). The end of the compound 'pāṭheśuvālubhiḥ' is doubtful; 'elavālu' is a conjectured correction of 'eśuvālu' and fits the 8 syllables of the half-line; it is not sure. The unit has no verb. 'kola' is read as the fruit; the other meaning (a unit of weight) is not adopted.

words.gloss: utpala (blue water lily, Nymphaea; probable); and the rest

hindi: दाह यानी जलन को नष्ट करने वाला, घी और दूध सहित; और दूसरा उत्पल आदि के साथ।
english: Destroying burning (dāha), with ghee and milk; and the second (one) with utpala (probably blue water lily) and the rest.
notes: GROUPING: continues 62. 'dvitīyaḥ' is 'the second', and what it is the second of is not stated (the unit speaks of two kinds that remove burning, the first with ghee and milk and the second with utpala and the rest). 'dāha' = burning (sensation). utpala: probable blue water lily (Nymphaea).

words.gloss: śālmali (silk-cotton tree, Bombax ceiba; see unit 60); stalks (vṛnta)

hindi: शाल्मली यानी सेमल के डंठलों की मुट्ठी भर, दूध में पकाई हुई, घी से युक्त।
english: A fistful of the stalks of śālmali (silk-cotton tree), cooked in milk, accompanied by ghee.
notes: GROUPING: 64 and 65 form one sentence ('hitaḥ pravāhaṇe' in 65). The gender of 'siddhaḥ' and 'anvitaḥ' (masculine) does not agree with 'muṣṭim' (feminine accusative); the grammar is loose, so the translation keeps the words as they stand.

words.gloss: in straining (pravāhaṇa; straining, as in tenesmus; standard)
of śālmalaka (taken as the silk-cotton tree, see unit 60)

hindi: प्रवाहण यानी जोर लगाने में हितकर; वैसे ही शाल्मलक के डंठलों से भी।
english: Beneficial in pravāhaṇa (straining); likewise with the stalks of śālmalaka.

text_flags.why: possible: 'dhṛnta' is not a word; the 'stalks' (vṛnta) of unit 64 are meant

notes: GROUPING: continues 64. The printed 'tadvaddhṛṃtaiḥ' is read as 'tadvad vṛntaiḥ' (as in 64 'vṛntānām'); flagged. 'śālmalaka' is taken as the same tree as śālmalī (probable). 'pravāhaṇa' = straining at stool (standard).

words.gloss: karbudāra (a Bauhinia, perhaps the white-flowered kovidāra or Bauhinia purpurea; disputed); āḍhakī (pigeon pea, Cajanus cajan; standard); nīpa (kadamba, Neolamarckia cadamba; probable); vidula (cane, Calamus rotang, or a willow, Salix; disputed)

hindi: दूध के साथ तैयार किए हुए कर्बुदार, आढकी यानी अरहर, नीप यानी प्रायः कदम्ब और विदुल से।
english: With karbudāra, āḍhakī (pigeon pea), nīpa (probably kadamba) and vidula, (ones) prepared with milk.

text_flags.why: possible: 'kīṃnapa' looks like a misprint of 'kīnīpa' (āḍhakī + nīpa)

notes: GROUPING: continues 65. The printed 'āḍhakīṃnapa' is read as 'āḍhakī-nīpa' (the group 'karbudāra, nīpa, vidula' recurs elsewhere in the book); flagged as possible. The unit has no verb and no noun for the condition; it is not stated what it is for.

words.gloss: śrīparṇī (probably Gmelina arborea; probable); kovidāra (orchid tree, Bauhinia variegata; probable); born of

hindi: परिकर्त यानी काटने वाली पीड़ा में, वैसे ही श्रीपर्णी यानी प्रायः गम्भारी और कोविदार यानी प्रायः कचनार से उत्पन्न डंठलों से।
english: In parikarta (cutting pain), likewise with the stalks born of śrīparṇī (probably Gmelina) and kovidāra (probably the orchid tree).
notes: GROUPING: continues 66. Normalisation: the printed 'parikartte' has a doubled t (-rtt- to -rt-). 'parikarta' is taken as 'cutting pain' (the condition parikartikā is its usual name; this is the standard reading). śrīparṇī is probable (Gmelina arborea, = kāśmarya); kovidāra probable.

words.gloss: unclear in the print (contains punarnav-); unsplit

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार: परिस्राव यानी बहने में, सिद्ध किया हुआ दूध; सदृशविपुनर्नवं जो छपाई में अस्पष्ट है।
english: On a conjectural reading: in parisrava (flowing out), cooked milk; sadṛśavipunarnava (unclear in the print; it appears to contain the name punarnavā).

text_flags.why: possible: the word does not parse; it may contain 'sadṛśa' and 'punarnava', but no reading is firm

notes: GROUPING: 68 and 69 go together (milk cooked with the drugs named in these two units). The last word 'sadṛśavipunarnavaṃ' cannot be restored with certainty (8 syllables, so the metre is complete); it may contain 'sadṛśa' ('similar') and a punarnavā name, so it is left unsplit and untranslated. 'parisrava' = flowing out (a discharge). The reading of the unit as a whole is low in confidence.

words.gloss: taṇḍulīyaka (a spiny amaranth, Amaranthus spinosus; probable); joined

hindi: आखुकर्णिका से, उसी प्रकार तण्डुलीयक यानी प्रायः चौलाई से युक्त की हुई।
english: With ākhukarṇikā (identity disputed), likewise, joined with taṇḍulīyaka (probably a spiny amaranth).
notes: GROUPING: continues 68. 'yuktayā' is feminine and agrees with ākhukarṇikayā. The statement is elliptical; the cooked milk of 68 is carried over but not stated here.

words.gloss: kākanāsā (lit. 'crow-nose'; identity disputed); rāja (royal); kaserukā (a sedge, Scirpus grossus; probable)

hindi: अश्वावरोहक, काकनासा और राजकसेरुका।
english: Aśvāvarohaka, kākanāsā and rājakaserukā (probably a royal sedge, Scirpus).
notes: GROUPING: continues 69; 70 and 71 go together ('siddhāḥ ... syuḥ'). aśvāvarohaka is unidentified; kākanāsā disputed; rājakaserukā probably a form of kaserukā (Scirpus grossus; probable).

words.gloss: honey (kṣaudra); añjana (a collyrium substance; which one is not stated; disputed); ghee (ghṛta)

hindi: अतियोग यानी अधिकता होने पर वे दूध में सिद्ध किए जाने चाहिए, शहद, अञ्जन और घी से युक्त।
english: In atiyoga (excess), they should be cooked in milk, joined with honey, añjana and ghee.
notes: GROUPING: continues 70 (the drugs of 70 are the subject). 'atiyoga' is kept as the Sanskrit term (excess); the text does not say excess of what. 'kṣīre' can be taken with 'siddhāḥ' (cooked in milk). añjana: a collyrium substance, which one is not stated (disputed).

words.gloss: nyagrodha (banyan, Ficus benghalensis; standard, the same tree as vaṭa of unit 56); beginning with

hindi: और न्यग्रोध यानी वट से आरम्भ होने वाले चार से; उसी विधि से दूसरा।
english: And with the four beginning with nyagrodha (banyan); by that very method, another.

text_flags.why: possible: 'bhiica' is not a form; 'caturbhiś ca' fits the sense and gives the 8-syllable pāda

notes: GROUPING: the sentence is not finished here; 72 closes this chunk and the list of four continues in the next chunk (unit 73 begins a list). The four are not named in the unit, so none is supplied. 'aparaḥ' = another (what is meant is not stated). The printed 'caturbhiica' is read as 'caturbhiś ca' (flagged).
